newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Three killed in explosion in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Three killed in explosion in Colombia.

text.p: A powerful explosion rocked the centre of Colombia's northwest city of Medellin on Wednesday, killing at least three people and injuring 14 others seriously, authorities said.

In the initial confusion there were conflicting accounts as to the cause of the blast, which occurred close to a popular restaurant called La Sorpresa and was attributed by some witnesses to the explosion of a gas cylinder.

National Police officials said it appeared to have been caused by a bomb. "It was a high-powered bomb apparently," said Gen. Luis Ernesto Gilibert, deputy director of the National Police. "Everything points to an act of terrorism," he said.
"It was extremely powerful," said Mauricio Restrepo, a business executive whose office is close to where the explosion occurred.
Alvaro Uribe, governor of Antioquia province of which Medellin is the capital, said police had confirmed at least three people were killed in the blast and said 14 others were seriously injured.
Radio reports spoke of as many as four dead and said up to 40 people were injured.
